clauses.mechanism: expiration_by_own_terms: age condition in the clause can no longer be met
clauses.reason: Section 3(a)(i) requires notice when the records are less than 10 years old and the submitter designated the information as confidential commercial information, and it applies only to information submitted before January 1, 1988. Under the clause own terms the youngest covered record, one submitted on December 31, 1987, reached an age of 10 years on December 31, 1997, so from that day no covered record can be less than 10 years old and the branch can no longer apply. The end is recorded on December 31, 1997 inclusive of the day the last covered record turned 10; the alternative reading that the branch ended on the last day on which a covered record was still under 10 years old, December 30, 1997, is disclosed. The source is the held text of the order itself (the whole original is the only own-terms source record the packet offers for this clause); the operative sentence is section 3(a)(i). Paragraph (ii) of section 3(a) is a separate branch with no age limit and is decided separately. This ending is by the order own terms and not by any later instrument.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12600 of June 23, 1987 (52 FR 23781, Federal Register Vol. 52 No. 122, Thursday June 25, 1987; FR Doc. 87-14602) establishes predisclosure notification procedures for confidential commercial information under the Freedom of Information Act. The held original is the machine-extracted text of the govinfo Federal Register PDF (pages 23781-23783) with title, preamble, Sections 1 to 10, the document number and the White House dateline present; one line after section 3(a)(ii) is cut at a page break and the order text as printed in the Code note (a lead whose bytes are not held) completes it, so the held text is read as cut off, not as changed. Identity and completeness were confirmed against the text. The U.S. Code search over release point 119-121 returned the order printed in full as a note to 5 U.S.C. 552; that machine lead is not cited as a source because its archive bytes are not held, so the current predicate cited for each operative clause is the held original clause text with the bounded searches (original-plus-bounded-search route). The eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 returned 153 hits that cite the order, showing wide agency use, but the claim rests on the held original text and the bounded searches. The only clause decided terminated is section 3(a)(i), whose own text limits it to records under 10 years old among information submitted before 1988, so it cannot apply after 1997-12-31; the first-end date and its inclusive reading are explained in that clause. The Federal Register catalogue search found no disposition note for this order, and the held later texts that cite the order number (agency rules and notices through 2026) apply it and do not amend or revoke it.
